title: Cohort safety: telemetry -> trigger matrix (working draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a proposal for a compact, actionable matrix that maps telemetry signals to automated and manual triggers for cohort-level canaries and A/B exposures. The goal is a repeatable contract teams can copy into feature playbooks so cross-functional owners (Product, Eng, SRE, Observability) can agree on what to watch, how to score signals, and what the immediate fallback semantics are.

Context / motivation (short):
- We run many small cohort canaries (0.1% -> 5%) across hosted, dedicated, and private tiers.
- Current rollouts rely on a scatter of dashboards and ad-hoc pager events. Hard to standardize when to pause, rollback, or expand.
- Need compact mapping: telemetry -> severity -> action -> owner -> SLAs for response.

Key constraints we must honor:
- Latency-sensitive features: prefer manual confirmation for rollback if 95p latency spike persists <5m but automatic throttling for sustained >10m.
- Cost-sensitive flows: when token-rate surges exceed budget, prefer automated scaling to cheaper model variant then pause expansion.
- Regulatory cohorts (enterprise privacy/region): require product + security sign-off for any rollback affecting audit logs.

Signal categories (examples):
1) Quality signals
   - Regression rate: % of responses flagged by evals or automated rerankers as failing guardrails
   - User dissatisfaction: NPS-like thumbs-down events, helpdesk tickets trend
2) Reliability signals
   - Error rate: 5xx/invalid-responses over baseline
   - Latency: p50/p95/p99 compared to baseline window
   - Model OOMs / node reboots
3) Resource/cost signals
   - Token throughput change vs expected
   - GPU utilization and queue length
   - Cost burn rate per cohort
4) Safety/abuse signals
   - Safety classifier spike (toxicity/PII/PHI triggers)
   - External reports or compliance exceptions
5) Telemetry health signals
   - Missing heartbeat, mismatched schema, KV cache corruption rate

Signal scoring heuristic (proposal):
- Each signal has a short window aggregation and a severity weight (1..5).
- Compute cohort-score = sum(weight * normalised-deviation). Normalised-deviation = (observed - baseline)/stdev-baseline but bounded to [0,5].
- Thresholds:
   - advisory (score 3–6): notify owners, increase sampling, hold expansion
   - action (score 7–12): automated mitigation (throttle new cohorts, reduce exposure by 50%, swap to fallback model) + oncall alert
   - critical (score >12): immediate full rollback and incident channel open

Trigger table (compact):
- Regression rate: advisory when +3pp above baseline; action when +7pp; critical when +15pp. Owner: Product/Applied ML. Actions: increase eval sampling; route traffic to last-good model; rollback if critical.
- Latency p95: advisory when +150ms; action when +400ms for >5min; critical when +1s sustained >2min. Owner: SRE/Serving runtime. Actions: autoscale/burst, if unavailable reduce batch size or fall back to cached responses.
- Error rate (5xx): advisory when x1.5 baseline; action when x3 baseline; critical when x5 baseline. Owner: SRE. Actions: circuit-breaker cohort, roll back gateway changes.
- Safety classifier spike: advisory at +2x baseline; action at +4x; critical at +10x OR any verified PII leak. Owner: Security + Product. Actions: pause cohort, hotpatch prompt guardrails, escrow logs for review.

Fallback contract primitives (what teams must agree on per rollout):
- Minimum required signals to enable automatic mitigation (e.g., must have live latency + error + safety classifier feeds).
- Fallback model variants and compatibility list (IDs) with explicit degradation expectations per variant.
- Cost-shift rules: whether cost mitigation is allowed to increase latency or reduce quality and by how much.
- Escalation list: primary owner, secondary, SRE oncall, security lead, and communication channels.
- Data retention for forensic review when rollback triggered.

Operational runbook snippets (for inclusion in rollouts):
- On advisory: open the cohort telemetry thread, set sampling to 10x, schedule a 30-min sync with owners, post initial observations and hypotheses in thread.
- On action: create a rollback MR if auto-rollback not configured; if configured, confirm auto-action executed and then run smoke tests against production canary cohort.
- On critical: execute rollback, create incident in incident system, assign postmortem owner, preserve all relevant telemetry snapshots.

Checklist for teams before enabling automatic actions (must be validated in Console):
- [ ] Live feeds: latency, errors, safety classifier, token-rate
- [ ] Baseline window defined (7d ideally) and stdev captured
- [ ] Fallback model verified on synthetic probes (smoke harness)
- [ ] Communication playbook assigned (names + Slack + email + oncall rotation)
- [ ] Audit controls enabled for private deployments

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve (short list):
- How do we weight correlated signals across cohorts (slice decorrelation)? Do we penalize global drift separately?
- Rollback churn: automatic rollbacks risk oscillations. Need a cool-down policy and canary memory (last N actions).
- Synthetic probes vs user signals: probes are faster but can diverge from real-user failure modes. What mix?
- SLA on human confirmation windows for non-critical actions (30m? 1h?).

Next steps / suggested owners:
- Draft proto in Console: Maya to add a JSON schema for per-feature trigger contract (due 2025-01-20).
- Telemetry onboarding checklist: Diego to document data feeds and event names in Confluence (due 2025-01-17).
- SRE: Priya to prototype automated throttle + fallback in staging for latency-trigger (RINF-4523) (due 2025-02-05).
- Applied ML: Tomislav to validate fallback model behavioral regressions on 10 curated prompts (due 2025-01-28).

Notes to self / rough heuristics scribbles:
- If cohort-score passes action threshold twice within a rolling 15m window => escalate to action phase.
- Add extra weight for safety signals on enterprise cohorts.
- Consider a separate "cost-exhaustion" quick action that reduces exposure but does not rollback quality (cheaper model swap).

Copyable template (single-paragraph summary to paste into new feature playbook):
"Telemetry-trigger contract: baseline window = 7d; required feeds = latency/errors/safety/token-rate; scoring = weighted normalized deviation (weights per-signal documented); action thresholds = advisory: 3-6, action: 7-12, critical: >12; automatic mitigations allowed only if fallback model and synthetic probe pass; on critical, immediate rollback + incident."

Appendix (useful refs):
- Existing canary dashboards: /dashboards/rollouts/canary-exposure (link in Console)
- RINF-4523 (SRE latency automation spike)
- Console PR #789 (draft UI for rollout contracts)

---
This is intentionally terse and operational: the goal is a small, copy-pasteable contract teams can attach to rollouts. Feedback welcome — ping @aisha or drop notes in #prod-rollouts.
